Messages.Author: skimflux
Messages.Body:
The current Trap discussion/suggestion reminded me of an observation that I've made ages ago: most players play cards to the playing area, even non-permanent cards, and only move them to the ash heap once it is no longer relevant to the current game state.

For example: when playing Cariorn Crows, it is common to leave the card in the playing area for the duration of the combat - strictly speaking the card should be simply shown to all players and moved to the ash heap immediately. Everybody understands that the card is actually in the ash heap and not 'in play', but it is a common way to remind everyone of the lingering effect of the card. This is specially useful for new players.

So I would like to propose an addition to the current rules that reflects the reality of how the cards are actually played: to create a 'temporary play area' where cards are put for the duration of their effect, but which is still part of the ash heap for gameplay purposes. This would act only as a reminder of which cards have been played (with no impact on current gameplay mechanics), and should be cleaned up at the end of every phase (ie, every card which has no effect beyond the current phase is moved to the 'permanent' ash heap).

What do you guys think?

Messages.Author: skimflux
Messages.Body:
That only applies to action cards - other card types are played to the ash heap (except when explicitly put in play).

1.6.1 (...)A card is played by placing it face up in the playing area or by showing it to the other players and placing it face up in the ash heap.(...)

6.1.6 (...)To take the action described on an action card in your hand, play the card and lock the acting minion. If the action is successful, it resolves as indicated on the card (and the cost, if any, is paid). If the action is unsuccessful, the card is burned.(...)

1.6.3. Minion Cards
Minion cards are cards that your vampires and allies (collectively referred to as "minions") play. Unless the card states otherwise, a minion card is burned after a minion plays it.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Correct. Only action cards are in limbo, waiting for resolution. All other cards are resolved immediately.

Messages.Author: skimflux
Messages.Body:
I understand that creating a new area may be troublesome, but the idea is to simply codify that convention. If you can do that without creating a new area, it would be even better - I just failed to see an easy way to do that.
I can see advantages in clarity mainly for combat and stealth/intercept interactions, both of which are very common in the game.

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body: I don't believe we need a new area either. However, we could make it a rule that all cards stay in play as long as they affect the game state. That would open a new design space for burning transient cards after they have been played.

Messages.Author: skimflux
Messages.Body: To leave cards in play would impact several things (Reality Mirror, Spiritual Guidance, etc), that's why I proposed it as a new subarea of the ash heap - this way it would not change any existing mechanics, but it would help to clarifiy the game state and could still open a new design space for future cards.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Correct. Only action cards are in limbo, waiting for resolution. All other cards are resolved immediately.
>
We could make change the rules so that cards that have an ongoing effect on the game state (such as carrion crows, etc) would be in limbo (kept in play) until the effect ends. This would make it easier to track game state. VTES has an awful lot of triggers and effects like this to track, and I feel that constantly checking and rechecking these to ensure you don't forget anything during the game will lead to slower play overall. Having things to help people track these in the heat of the game would probably make the game proceed more smoothly. People do this already, even though it isn't official.
